title: Chronic Diarrhoea in Paediatrics
subject: Paediatrics
summary: Chronic diarrhoea (>4 weeks) in children is a diagnostic challenge in low‑resource settings. A systematic approach—history, exam, targeted tests—helps identify infectious, inflammatory, osmotic or malabsorptive causes and guide management.

sections.p: Chronic diarrhoea is loose stools >4 weeks, or >3 stools/day for >4 weeks. Diagnosis requires ruling out acute causes and confirming persistence.
Use the WHO malnutrition and dehydration scales; classify as mild, moderate or severe based on weight loss, dehydration signs and growth faltering.
In East Africa, infections dominate. Follow a hierarchy: infectious, inflammatory, malabsorptive, osmotic, medication‑related.

faq.q: What is the first test to order in a child with chronic diarrhoea in a low‑resource setting?
faq.a: Stool microscopy for parasites and bacterial culture, as these are common and inexpensive.

faq.q: How do you differentiate osmotic from secretory diarrhoea?
faq.a: Calculate fecal osmotic gap; a gap >200 mOsm/kg suggests osmotic, <200 mOsm/kg suggests secretory.

faq.q: Why is oral rehydration solution preferred over IV fluids in most cases?
faq.a: It corrects electrolytes, is inexpensive, can be given orally, and reduces hospital stay.

exam: What is the most likely cause of chronic diarrhoea in a 5‑year‑old boy from a rural East African village with weight loss and night‑time diarrhoea? — Consider parasitic infections (Giardia, Cryptosporidium, Isospora) and malaria; order stool microscopy and malaria test.

A child presents with chronic diarrhoea and blood in stool. Which investigation would you order first and why? — Fecal calprotectin to rule out inflammatory bowel disease; if high, proceed to colonoscopy.
You suspect HIV enteropathy in a child with chronic diarrhoea. What is the next step in management? — Perform a rapid HIV test; if positive, start ART and consider prophylaxis.

A child has chronic diarrhoea but normal stool microscopy and cultures. What is the next diagnostic step? — Measure fecal fat to assess malabsorption; if positive, consider celiac disease or pancreatic insufficiency.
Why should you avoid giving antibiotics empirically in chronic diarrhoea? — It can worsen dysbiosis, cause resistance, and mask underlying causes.
A child with chronic diarrhoea is dehydrated. Which fluid should you give first? — Oral rehydration solution; if severe, start IV isotonic saline.
What is the key difference between osmotic and secretory diarrhoea on stool osmotic gap? — Osmotic gap >200 mOsm/kg indicates osmotic; <200 mOsm/kg indicates secretory.
When is surgical referral indicated in chronic diarrhoea? — Persistent bloody diarrhoea, failure to respond to medical therapy, or evidence of obstruction or perforation.
